BiSCaL: bivariate separable causal effects in longitudinal studies

Source: R/BiSCaL-package.R
BiSCaL-package.Rd

Causal inference for two ordinal (including binary) responses measured repeatedly over time, for example two cholesterol measures in a clinical trial, when the responses may be missing intermittently and follow-up may be censored. BiSCaL implements the methods of Hu and Yi (2026). The treatment \(A\) is conceptualized as two components, \(A_1\) acting on the first response and \(A_2\) on the second (\(A = a\) corresponds to \(A_1 = A_2 = a\)). Effects are defined at the end time point \(K\) through generalized odds ratios (GOR) of the two responses: the total treatment effect \(TTE_K\) compares \((A_1, A_2) = (1, 1)\) with \((0, 0)\), and the separable treatment effect \(STE_{j,K}\) changes only the component acting on response \(j\); they satisfy \(STE_{1,K} + STE_{2,K} = 2\,TTE_K\).

Workflow

  1. Arrange the data in long format, one row per subject and visit, with the visit index 0, 1, ..., K, the treatment and baseline covariates; code missing responses as NA (see simtrial for an example).

  2. Fit the transition and baseline models with biscal(); inspect them with summary() (biscal-methods).

  3. Estimate and test the effects for given covariate values with aste(), or averaged over a covariate distribution with easte(); gor() and cf_prob() give the underlying generalized odds ratios and counterfactual distributions. Plot effects over follow-up with plot.biscal_aste().

simulate_biscal(), biscal_coefs() and biscal_truth() reproduce the simulation designs of the paper. See vignette("BiSCaL") for a worked analysis.

References

Hu, P. and Yi, G. Y. (2026). Inference about separable causal effects with longitudinal bivariate ordinal responses with missingness and censoring. Statistics in Medicine, 45, e70320. doi:10.1002/sim.70320
